Tap the blank area to exit one-handed mode
Swipe up to go Home or open Recents while keeping one-handed mode active. Turn off to swipe up to exit one-handed mode.
Tap the side to switch sides
When on, tapping the blank area above the screen still exits, while tapping the blank area on the side switches one-handed mode to the other side. When off, tapping any blank area exits.
Swipe up or down on the blank area beside the screen: up enlarges, down shrinks. The scale is saved on release, and a preset becomes a custom scale.

Show the dashed outlines of the two blank strips, and what a tap or a drag there does, for a couple of seconds after entering. Turning it off keeps the outline that appears while the side strip is being dragged.
With this off the module never touches the system switch, so opening this app leaves it exactly as you set it. Turn it on if you want the switch to be kept on, which is what the edge gesture needs.

With this off the module broadcasts nothing, which is harder to detect; the launcher then keeps its swipe region on the original screen area, so a swipe up from the app\'s own bottom edge lands in the wrong place.

What fills the blank area outside the scaled screen: a solid color, the system wallpaper or your own picture. A solid color follows the system theme by default; presets, the color wheel and a 6-digit hex value are all available.
Checking system support and LSPosed status
Enable the module in LSPosed, select System Framework and SystemUI, then restart your device.

With gesture navigation enabled, swipe down from the bottom gesture bar while your device is unlocked and in portrait orientation. On Xiaomi devices, you can also swipe down from the bottom gesture area when the gesture bar is hidden.\n\nSwipe down on the left half to anchor the screen at the bottom left, or on the right half to anchor it at the bottom right.

Tap the blank area above the scaled screen to exit. By default, swiping up from the bottom gesture bar also exits one-handed mode.

With “Tap the side to switch sides” enabled, tapping the blank area on the side switches to the other side instead of exiting, while the top area still exits.

Enable “Keep Home and Recents gestures” to swipe up to go Home or open Recents while keeping one-handed mode active. Use the top blank area to exit.

The blank side area holds a column of buttons: More at the bottom opens Settings and Exit one-handed mode above it and pushes the Back button up. Back is always visible and does what the system back key does. Rotating the screen or turning it off also exits one-handed mode.

The blank area outside the scaled screen has two parts: the top strip across the whole width, and the side strip on the left or right.

By default every tap in the blank area exits one-handed mode. With “Tap the side to switch sides” enabled, the top strip still exits while the side strip slides the scaled screen straight across to the other side, without returning to full screen first.

“Surround color” changes the fill color of that area and follows the system theme background by default. Pick a preset or enter a 6-digit hex value such as 1C1C1E. The change applies immediately, including while one-handed mode is active.

Swipe up or down on the blank area beside the scaled screen to resize it continuously: up enlarges, down shrinks. Dragging about 45% of the screen height changes the scale by 60 points, clamped to 20%–90%.

A drag has to clear 16dp before it starts; anything shorter is still treated as a tap, which switches sides or exits.

The scale is saved on release: a preset becomes a custom scale.

Turn off “Drag the side to resize” in the settings to disable the gesture.

The scale is the width and height of the smaller screen as a percentage of the original. At 70%, both dimensions are 70% of their original size. The content and corner radius scale proportionally.

The presets are 80%, 70%, and 60%; you can also drag the slider between 20% and 90%. A smaller value brings more of the screen within reach. The slider, the presets and a vertical drag on the side strip all share one value and stay in sync. Changes apply the next time you enter one-handed mode; if it is already active, the content animates smoothly to the new scale.

Dragging the slider only previews the value, which is applied on release. Applying it live would move the screen and the slider at the same time and make fine adjustments impossible.

After enabling the module and restarting, another app can send a broadcast with action io.githuh.onehandedmode.action.START to package com.android.systemui. The sender needs no root or system permission.

Shell command:
am broadcast -a io.githuh.onehandedmode.action.START -p com.android.systemui

The screen opens on the right by default. Add --es side left to open on the left, or --es side right for the right. The current scale applies. Repeated requests keep an active mode open. Entry requires an unlocked device in portrait orientation, as with gestures.
Use the current system wallpaper and follow wallpaper changes
Pick a picture from your gallery to fill the area outside the screen
0% keeps the original; higher values approach the blur behind Recents
